title: Hydrodynamic memory in overdamped colloidal dynamics
authors: Benjamin Sorkin, Günther Turk, Howard A. Stone
abstract: Micron-sized colloid particles diffusing through a fluid experience hydrodynamic inertial and memory effects, the latter causing velocity autocorrelation to decay as a power law. At the same time, many theoretical descriptions treat colloidal diffusion in a fluid using overdamped Langevin dynamics for its convenience, eliminating velocity, omitting inertia, but also ignoring the power-law memory. In this Letter, we show that hydrodynamic memory survives in the overdamped (colloid-inertialess) limit. By identifying the dimensionless parameter controlling the crossover between early- and late-time dynamics, we derive in closed form the overdamped Langevin equation in the presence of hydrodynamic memory. This provides a theoretical framework for realistically describing colloidal dynamics in a fluid, and establishes a rigorous basis for the positional memory observed in high-resolution experiments. Our theory predicts that hydrodynamic memory becomes increasingly pronounced for smaller particles and under stronger external forcing, and offers experimental probes for the crossover from conventional exponential relaxation to memory-dominated power-law dynamics.
summary: This work theoretically proves that hydrodynamic memory, characterized by a power-law decay, survives even when simplifying the dynamics to the overdamped (inertialess) limit for colloidal particles. By deriving a closed-form Basset-Langevin equation, the authors provide a more accurate description of particle motion than conventional models. This is crucial for interpreting high-resolution experiments that observe long-time positional correlations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fate of power-law hydrodynamic memory in the overdamped (inertialess) limit for colloidal particle dynamics.
main_result: The authors derive a closed-form, overdamped Basset-Langevin equation that successfully incorporates hydrodynamic memory, showing it persists even when particle inertia is neglected.
method: The primary method involves performing a small-$\epsilon$ expansion on the full equation of motion, eliminating the velocity variable to derive the final memory-inclusive equation.
model_or_system: The system is micron-sized colloid particles diffusing through a fluid, modeled using Langevin dynamics that accounts for Stokes drag, added mass, and a power-law Basset memory term.
key_observables: Velocity autocorrelation function (expected power-law decay $\sim t^{-3/2}$), Mean-squared displacement (MSD), and positional autocorrelation functions.
important_parameters: The dimensionless parameter $\epsilon$ controls the crossover between early-time (exponential) and late-time (power-law) dynamics; smaller particles enhance memory effects.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system operates in the low-Reynolds-number, incompressible flow limit, and the standard overdamped model is insufficient as it ignores power-law memory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hierarchy of time scales, showing how the theory incorporating Basset memory predicts a crossover from conventional exponential relaxation to memory-dominated power-law decay.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the full underdamped equation to the overdamped limit via small-$\epsilon$ expansion, deriving the final Basset-Langevin equation, and then applying this theory to predict measurable long-time correlations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the rigorous derivation of memory effects in the low-Reynolds number limit provides a powerful theoretical framework for understanding non-Markovian dynamics, which has parallels in open quantum systems and quantum dissipation.
